d1-flow.fact: The tool/call event is appended to the session log before pipeline.prepare runs, so logging comes before pre-execute policy.
d1-flow.fail_if: The diagram places the tool/call log entry after the policy, approval or guard check.

d1-flow.fact: Whether tool/call is logged does not depend on the policy decision: it depends only on the batch having a log target, which the agent loop always supplies.
d1-flow.fail_if: The diagram logs tool/call only on the allow branch, only on the approval branch, or only when policy asks.

d1-flow.fact: A denied or cancelled-by-policy call does not start the tool body but still produces an error result that goes through completion and is committed as tool/result.
d1-flow.fail_if: The diagram runs the tool body after a denial, or ends a denied call with no result returned to the model.

d1-flow.fact: An allowed call passes prepare (tools/pre-execute and guards), then dispatch (tools/execute wrapping the tool body), then complete (tools/post-execute), and only then the tool/result commit.
d1-flow.fail_if: The diagram runs post-execute before the tool body, runs pre-execute after the body, or commits tool/result before post-execute.

d1-flow.fact: Results commit in model order: a later call that settles first waits until all earlier slots have committed.
d1-flow.fail_if: The diagram commits or returns results in completion order, or shows faster parallel calls committing ahead of earlier calls.

d1-flow.fact: Only dispatch overlaps: prepare runs one call at a time in model order, and a call that is not classified parallel, including an unknown tool, runs as an exclusive barrier.
d1-flow.fail_if: The diagram runs policy checks concurrently for a batch, or runs every tool call in parallel with no exclusive path.

d1-flow.fact: Results reach the model indirectly: tool/result is appended to the session, the batch returns to the step loop, and the next step derives its request messages from the session, unless a result concludes the turn.
d1-flow.fail_if: The diagram sends the result straight from the tool or executor to the model with no session append and no new model request.

d2-impact.fact: JSONL storage does not own the event format: it encodes through the session-format catalog's current encoder, restores through catalog codecs, and refuses on load any event type outside the known set unless it is marked ignorable.
d2-impact.fail_if: The diagram shows JSONL storage as unaffected opaque storage, or shows unknown required event types being skipped silently on load.

d2-impact.fact: Every historical format has its own codec, and migration runs only through adjacent version steps; a missing step fails catalog construction.
d2-impact.fail_if: The diagram migrates an old version directly to current in one jump, or shows one shared decoder for all versions with no per-version codec or migration.

d2-impact.fact: For a historical log, events are decoded and migrated first, and validation of the current-format artifact runs on the migration output.
d2-impact.fail_if: The diagram validates historical events against the current schema before migration, or feeds them to consumers with no migration step.

d2-impact.fact: Session state and projections are derived from the event log: restore replays each event through the surface manager, projections fold events, and a persisted projection row is only a shortcut discarded on a stateVersion mismatch.
d2-impact.fail_if: The diagram treats reconstruction or projections as independent of event shape, or makes the projection cache an authoritative source that survives a version mismatch.

d2-impact.fact: The session controller passes committed events to the wire with no conversion, and the client checks the envelope, so a format change reaches clients directly.
d2-impact.fail_if: The diagram shows a translation layer that isolates clients from the log event shape, or shows clients as unaffected.

d2-impact.fact: Direct readers such as Markdown export and session commands take restored events, branch on event.type, read event.data themselves with no shared adapter, and let unmatched types pass silently.
d2-impact.fail_if: The diagram routes all direct readers through one central event adapter, shows them failing on every unhandled type, or shows them parsing raw JSONL files.

d2-impact.fact: The known event type set and the format catalog assembly are generated files produced by scripts, so a format change requires regeneration and not a hand edit.
d2-impact.fail_if: The diagram shows these catalogs as hand-maintained, or as inputs that the event format change does not touch.

d3-state.fact: The connection status has exactly six states: connecting, connected, reconnecting, waiting-credentials, failed and closed; gave-up, reconnect-disabled and unclosed-generation are reasons of failed.
d3-state.fail_if: The diagram adds a published state outside this set, such as disconnected or idle, or attaches gave-up, reconnect-disabled or unclosed-generation to a state other than failed.

d3-state.fact: After a loss, the generation is closed first and reconnect is scheduled only if closure is confirmed; unconfirmed closure gives failed with reason unclosed-generation and no reconnect.
d3-state.fail_if: The diagram goes from connected to reconnecting before cleanup with no closure check, or retries after unclosed-generation.

d3-state.fact: With reconnect disabled, a lost or failed connection goes to failed with reason reconnect-disabled and schedules no retry.
d3-state.fail_if: The diagram enters reconnecting or sets a retry timer when reconnect is disabled.

d3-state.fact: When consecutive failed attempts exceed maxAttempts, the tools are unregistered, the status becomes failed with reason gave-up, and no further timer is set.
d3-state.fail_if: The diagram retries forever, keeps retrying after gave-up, or leaves the budget-exhausted path out of a retry loop by showing no exit.

d3-state.fact: Reconnecting is only a backoff wait: its timer starts a new generation in connecting, success then gives connected, and a failed attempt returns to reconnecting or a failed state.
d3-state.fail_if: The diagram goes directly from reconnecting to connected with no connecting state.

d3-state.fact: A missing credential template value gives waiting-credentials with no retry timer, and a changed credential binding starts a new connecting generation with a reset attempt count.
d3-state.fail_if: The diagram sends missing credentials through the backoff retry loop, or shows waiting-credentials with no exit on a credential change.

d3-state.fact: Dispose stops timers, closes the current generation, unregisters tools and publishes closed, and it is the only path to closed.
d3-state.fail_if: The diagram reaches closed from a connection loss or from gave-up without dispose, or reconnects from closed.

d4-compare.fact: Standard is the shipped default preset, and a user-selected default in settings overrides it.
d4-compare.fail_if: The diagram marks PTC, Minimal or Creator as the shipped default.

d4-compare.fact: PTC differs from Standard in its rows by adding tool-executor-ptc, disabling workflow-ptc and tool-workflow, and disabling the plugin-manager tool; Standard has no executor row and uses the deployment's native executor.
d4-compare.fail_if: The diagram gives Standard the PTC executor, or gives PTC an active workflow tool or plugin-manager tool.

d4-compare.fact: Minimal mounts only a complete persona, tool-fs with read, write and edit off and readImage on, a compaction group and a persistent shell group; it lacks subagent, workflow, web, todo, skill, plan-mode and plugin-manager rows.
d4-compare.fail_if: The diagram gives Minimal subagents, web, todo, skills, plan mode or plugin management, or shows it with file edit and write tools on.

d4-compare.fact: Creator is the preset with id cordis, and it has Standard's rows plus tool-cordis and a skill-filesystem with extra custom skill directories.
d4-compare.fail_if: The diagram gives tool-cordis to another shipped preset, or shows Creator without the standard task tools.

d4-compare.fact: The plugin-manager tool is conditional on profileContext in Standard and Creator; the plugin-market tool row is off in Standard and PTC, and in Creator it needs profileContext and registers its tool only while the pluginMarket service is mounted, which an optional bundle supplies.
d4-compare.fail_if: The diagram gives plugin management to all presets unconditionally, gives Standard the market tool, or shows Creator's market tool as always available.

d4-compare.fact: Built-in PTC and Minimal are offered only with Coding Tools on; with Coding Tools off, the picker and roster hide them and a hidden default is reset to Standard, while Standard and Creator stay offered.
d4-compare.fail_if: The diagram gates Standard or Creator on Coding Tools, or shows PTC and Minimal as always available.

d4-compare.fact: Presets do not inherit from each other: each declares its own complete plugins list and the preset schema has no parent or extends field.
d4-compare.fail_if: The diagram draws inheritance or extends arrows between presets, such as Creator or PTC extending Standard at runtime.

d5-steps.fact: A typed manual install is inspected by the Host before installBundle, and a refused spec returns to the input form with nothing installed.
d5-steps.fail_if: The diagram runs pnpm before the spec check, or continues to install after a refused inspection.

d5-steps.fact: Manual install sends enabled as subject.selection ?? false, so a typed install does not activate the bundle, and enabling is a separate later user action through setBundleEnabled.
d5-steps.fail_if: The diagram shows a manual install activating the bundle automatically after pnpm with no separate enable step.

d5-steps.fact: package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml are saved before pnpm runs, and a final pnpm failure restores them and ends with a failed result, with no selection or reload; a registry-attributed failure with registries left first restores and tries the next registry.
d5-steps.fail_if: The diagram continues to selection or reload after the final pnpm failure, or shows no file restore on failure.

d5-steps.fact: After pnpm succeeds, the Host confirms a single added dependency, a bundle manifest, version compatibility and readable patches, and a failure of any of these also restores the files.
d5-steps.fail_if: The diagram selects or loads the bundle before these checks, or shows a failed check that leaves the saved files unrestored.

d5-steps.fact: selectBundle runs only when options.enabled is not false, and it writes the bundle into the profile selection before the reload step; the reload still runs when enabled is false.
d5-steps.fail_if: The diagram always runs selectBundle after install, or reloads before writing the selection.

d5-steps.fact: The platform check runs in selectBundle, outside the restore catch, so a platform refusal fails at the enable stage and leaves the installed dependency in place with no file restore.
d5-steps.fail_if: The diagram checks the platform before pnpm, or restores package.json and the lockfile after a platform refusal.

d5-steps.fact: With no HMR service the change is saved but not live: the result is restart-required with reason no-hmr and takes effect at restart; with HMR, reconcileProfile applies it live, unless it reports a required restart.
d5-steps.fail_if: The diagram shows the plugin live with no restart when HMR is absent, or shows a restart as always required when HMR is present.
